<!-- Generated by sync-kit from factory-kit 0.12.0. Edit plugins/factory-kit in solo-factory, not this copy. -->

Ship the current work. Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

Each step below is a factory-kit skill. Read its `SKILL.md` and follow it, passing on the relevant
arguments (`--base`, `--draft`, the ticket). Don't re-implement a step from memory. Keep a short
checklist of the steps so progress is visible.

| # | Step | Instructions | Skippable |
| - | ---- | ------------ | --------- |
| 1 | Branch | `.claude/skills/factory-checkout-branch/SKILL.md` (only if HEAD is on a shared branch, as defined in its step 1: protected branches, origin default, `CLAUDE.md` targets, CI push branches) | no |
| 2 | Format, lint, typecheck | `.claude/skills/factory-check/SKILL.md` | no |
| 3 | Tests (check coverage, fill gaps) | `.claude/skills/factory-test/SKILL.md` | `tests` |
| 4 | Review | `.claude/skills/factory-review/SKILL.md` | `review` |
| 5 | Docs | `.claude/skills/factory-update-docs/SKILL.md` | `docs` |
| 6 | Re-check | step 2 again, but only if steps 3–5 changed files | no |
| 7 | Verify | `.claude/skills/factory-verify/SKILL.md` (it skips itself when nothing runnable changed) | `verify` |
| 8 | Commit | `.claude/skills/factory-commit/SKILL.md`. Screenshots under `docs/evidence/<N>/` get their own `docs(evidence): screenshots for #<N>` commit | no |
| 9 | Follow-ups | See "Follow-ups" below | `mr` |
| 10 | MR description | `.claude/skills/factory-describe-pr/SKILL.md` | `mr` |
| 11 | Merge request | `.claude/skills/factory-create-pr/SKILL.md` | `mr` |

**Follow-ups** (step 9): collect every review finding left unfixed, every `not verified` area the
user accepted, and every follow-up the work names. Show the list and ask once. On a yes, create one
issue for each, labelled `inbox`, with `gh api` as in the intake skill's **GitHub calls**.

Write each issue in the repo's issue template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`), so intake can
take it without a round of questions. Use one `### <label>` heading per field, in the template's
order, and fill every required field:
- the user story names who the gap hurts;
- the acceptance criteria are Given/When/Then for the fixed behaviour;
- the scope names the apps it touches;
- the non-goals keep it as small as the finding.

Below the template's fields, state the finding, link the branch, and say why it was left. Pass the
issue numbers to `describe-pr`. A follow-up must not appear in the PR without its issue number.
With nothing to file, say so and go on.

Rules for the run:

- **Start**: if there is no change at all (no uncommitted work and no commits ahead of the base),
  say so and stop.
- **Stop on failure**: a failing check, failing test, or `blocker` review finding stops the
  pipeline. Report what failed and what is left. The user can re-run `/factory-ship` after fixing
  it, and finished steps are cheap to repeat.
- **Review findings**: show them and ask which to fix before moving on. Fix each chosen finding
  test first: write a test that fails without the fix, run it to see it fail, then fix. When no
  test tool in the repo can check it, say so in the PR. Then continue from step 6.
- **Verify**: a `fail` stops the pipeline like a failing test. If the user wants it fixed, fix it,
  then continue from step 6 (re-check), which runs verify again. For `not verified` areas, give the
  reason and ask whether to commit anyway.
- **Human gates**: the commit step asks before committing and the merge request step asks before
  pushing. Never skip those questions, even if the user said "ship it" at the start.
- **No remote** (`git remote` is empty): run steps 1–8 and 10, then explain that steps 9 and 11 need
  an `origin` remote on GitHub (or GitLab), and stop there.
- **End**: a summary table with each step, its result (done / skipped / failed / not reached), and
  the key output: branch name, files fixed, tests added and their result, findings fixed or open,
  docs changed, commits, MR URL.
